title: Engram current architecture and operator-console claim ledger

console_route_ledger_model.note: Each console_routes entry below records independent axes. page_source=present proves only that a Nuxt page file exists; it never sets journey_status=accepted by itself.

fields.page_source: present | absent — whether a matching apps/operator-console/pages/*.vue file exists
fields.deployment_forms: the distinct ways this route can be reached: standalone-nuxt (dedicated Compose service, port 3000), embedded-server (Go server serves the generated static bundle at its own origin), proxied-external (ENGRAM_OPERATOR_CONSOLE_URL reverse-proxy)
fields.direct_load_status: per deployment form: for standalone-nuxt/proxied-external, ok means locally replayed as loading the intended page. For embedded-server, ok means routing-verified — grep-confirmed no competing route registers this path ahead of the SPA catch-all in service.go; it is NOT a browser-load replay unless the evidence field also cites a passing HTTP-level test. collision means a same-path server route intercepts the request before the SPA fallback (proven, not inferred, when a test exists). untested-locally means not locally replayable in this batch.
fields.capability_status: live | flag-gated | convergence-in-progress | tombstone, applied to the backing capability/API this route depends on
fields.journey_status: accepted (a full source+runtime+browser-checked operator workflow) | partial (some reads/actions verified, others not) | blocked (a known collision or missing backend prevents the workflow) | not-applicable (informational-only page, no workflow to accept)
fields.activation: env var or flag gating the backing capability, when applicable
fields.limitations: known caveats: redirects, missing routes, unverifiable-locally notes
fields.evidence: repository-relative file(s) and, where useful, line ranges

architecture.claim: The agent host reaches Engram over a local stdio daemon, which connects to the server over gRPC.
Lifecycle hooks use the server REST API independently of the local MCP daemon.
The worker listener multiplexes REST and gRPC through cmux.
The server serves its generated console bundle by default and can proxy browser routes to ENGRAM_OPERATOR_CONSOLE_URL; Compose also runs the Nuxt console as a separate service.
Operator credentials stay on the server host while workstations use distinct database-backed tokens.
Server HTTP MCP, server SSE/Streamable-HTTP MCP, and a stdio-to-SSE bridge are not current setup paths.
architecture.note: A stale comment or test string is not route registration. The current MCP adapter is served through gRPC.

architecture.claim: Reranking is an optional configured recall path, not a default documented capability.
architecture.note: Source initializes this path when configured, but repository source cannot prove a deployment enabled it.

console_routes.task: Access administration (providers, invitations, users, roles, sessions, audit)

embedded-server.note: No server route registers "/access" ahead of the SPA catch-all at internal/worker/service.go:1540, so this path reaches the console shell, not a machine handler.

console_routes.auth: requireReady group with global auth middleware; console treats 401/403 responses as `forbidden` and locks the page
console_routes.limitations: This route is the live access-administration read/admin surface (providers, invitations, users, roles, sessions, audit log per apps/operator-console/composables/useOperatorAccess.ts). It is NOT a keycard-issuance workflow: creating an invitation here differs from the daemon's fatal-error text pointing operators at a `/tokens` page that does not exist in this console (see the Legacy /tokens limitations entry below). Treat invitation/session/user administration as live; treat keycard issuance as convergence-in-progress and unaccepted.
Backend job-status polling (POST /api/books, GET /api/books/{id}/status) exists; no browser replay of a full ingestion run in this batch.
CRUD/read/history/comment endpoints are registered and reachable; no browser replay in this batch.

embedded-server.note: No competing server route at "/graph"; the page loads regardless of flag state, but its data calls will be rejected until the flag is enabled.

console_routes.auth: requireReady group, global auth middleware, plus the graph flag gate on each handler
console_routes.limitations: The page renders at direct load in every deployment form; its underlying node/edge/traverse calls return disabled behavior until ENGRAM_GRAPH_ENABLED=true. journey_status=blocked until a flag-on browser replay is recorded.

standalone-nuxt.note: The dedicated Nuxt service on port 3000 has no competing machine route at "/health", so this form is expected to load pages/health.vue, but was not locally replayed.

embedded-server.note: internal/worker/service.go:1300 registers s.router.Get("/health", s.handleHealth) BEFORE the SPA catch-all at line 1540. chi matches the more specific static route first, so a direct browser load of http://<server-origin>/health returns the machine health JSON body ({"status":...,"version":...}), never pages/health.vue. Confirmed locally: internal/worker/static_health_route_collision_test.go asserts the embedded route body is JSON, not the SPA shell.

proxied-external.note: Depends on how the external upstream itself is fronted; not replayable without one.

console_routes.auth: the /health path itself is listed in TokenAuth.ExemptPaths (internal/worker/middleware.go:240), so the embedded machine-health handler requires no auth; the page's own data sources (/api/selfcheck, /api/stats/vnext, /api/vector/metrics, /api/update/status, /api/migrations, /api/flags) sit behind the requireReady group and global auth middleware once the collision above is worked around
console_routes.limitations: Do not teach '/health' as a working embedded-console page until the collision is repaired (route rename, path split, or machine-health move to /api/health-only). Standalone Nuxt is the only deployment form where this page is expected to load, and even that was not locally confirmed in this batch.

console_routes.auth: requireReady group, global auth middleware; no admin-only gate observed in internal/worker/handlers_rules.go, so any authenticated identity (session or client keycard) can list/create/enable/update/delete rules

requireReady group, global auth middleware; /api/context/search is POST-callable by read-only client keycards via the readOnlyAllowedPosts allowlist (internal/worker/middleware.go:162-165) since it does not mutate state

requireReady group, global auth middleware; handlers_vault.go has no additional IsSessionAdmin/role gate beyond the global middleware, so any authenticated identity (session or client keycard) can list/store/delete vault credentials and read decrypted values via GET /api/vault/credentials/{name}
the /settings page itself makes no fetch call; the general-settings modal it opens reads/writes /api/config and /api/flags, both behind the requireReady group and global auth middleware
console_routes.limitations: pages/settings.vue is not a configuration page. On mount it calls openSettingsModal('general') and, when the current route is exactly '/settings', immediately router.replace('/'). Deep-linking or refreshing on /settings opens the general-settings modal over the overview page rather than showing settings content at a stable /settings URL; there is no separate settings screen to browse back to.

limitations.subject: Localized README files
limitations.note: English README is canonical until localization parity is restored. See README.md's canonical-documentation notice for the visible stale/non-canonical links to both files.

limitations.subject: Legacy /tokens text
limitations.note: The daemon's fatal-token diagnostic and its --help text still name a dashboard '/tokens' route. The promoted console has no matching page file; the closest live route is /access, which is an administration surface, not an issuance wizard. internal/config/envnames.go's EnvWorkstationToken doc-comment previously repeated the same stale '/tokens UI' phrasing; it has been corrected in this batch to point at the actual issuance endpoint (POST /api/auth/tokens). Do not treat the daemon text as proof of a working /tokens page.

limitations.subject: Embedded /health direct-load collision
limitations.note: P0: fix before teaching the embedded console's /health page as a working operator route. The machine health handler is registered ahead of the SPA catch-all, so the embedded server form always serves JSON at this path instead of pages/health.vue.

limitations.subject: Operator-console package not installed in this worktree
limitations.note: apps/operator-console/node_modules is absent in this batch's worktree. Standalone-Nuxt and proxied-external direct-load replay for every route above is recorded as untested-locally because `npm install` was not run offline in this batch. Embedded-server direct_load_status="ok" rows are a route-registration grep against service.go (confirming no competing handler intercepts the path before the SPA catch-all), not a browser-load or live-HTTP replay; only /health has an actual HTTP-level test (static_health_route_collision_test.go) proving its collision.
